title: Booking clicks
description:
Clicks on the Book now CTAs, counted server-side by the /go/airbnb Worker and written to the booking_clicks Analytics Engine dataset.

blob1 ?src= page, blob2 referer, blob3 country, blob4 ?pos= placement, blob5 bot verdict, blob6 user agent, blob7 network operator. Fields are appended and never inserted, so rows written before a field existed simply carry fewer blobs -- blob5 = '' means unclassified, not human.

Everything except 'Recent clicks' counts only clicks classified as coming from a browser, which means the numbers start on 2026-08-20. Earlier rows carry no verdict and are excluded rather than assumed human. The Conversion row additionally requires a real placement, and divides by visits from Web Analytics over GraphQL.

options.content:
**Clicks have only been classified since 2026-08-20 23:37 UTC** (ISS-36), and every panel below except *Recent clicks* counts classified browser clicks only. Empty panels mean no real clicks have landed since then, not a broken query — check *Recent clicks*, which is unfiltered.

Earlier rows are still in the dataset and are deliberately not counted. The two weeks before that date are dominated by probes, DNS drain checks and crawlers following the booking link, and nothing in the row distinguishes those from a person.

panels.title: Clicks in range

defaults.noValue: No classified clicks in this range

targets.query:
SELECT
    SUM(_sample_interval) AS clicks
FROM booking_clicks
WHERE $timeFilter AND blob5 = 'human' AND blob1 NOT IN ('/canary/', '/verify-iss36/')

panels.description:
Excludes clicks classified as bots (blob5), the monitor canary, and the ISS-36 verification rows.

Counts only clicks the Worker classified as coming from a browser, so the series starts on 2026-08-20. Rows written before that carry no verdict and are excluded rather than assumed human -- the two weeks before it are dominated by probes, DNS drain checks and crawler traffic, and there is no way to tell which of those rows were people. 'Recent clicks' is left unfiltered so the classifier can be audited.

panels.title: Clicks over time by page
panels.description:
One series per ?src= value. Counted with SUM(_sample_interval), which is how Analytics Engine undoes sampling.

Counts only clicks the Worker classified as coming from a browser, so the series starts on 2026-08-20. Rows written before that carry no verdict and are excluded rather than assumed human -- the two weeks before it are dominated by probes, DNS drain checks and crawler traffic, and there is no way to tell which of those rows were people. 'Recent clicks' is left unfiltered so the classifier can be audited.

defaults.noValue: No classified clicks in this range

targets.query:
SELECT
    $timeSeries AS t,
    blob1 AS src,
    SUM(_sample_interval) AS clicks
FROM booking_clicks
WHERE $timeFilter AND blob5 = 'human' AND blob1 NOT IN ('/canary/', '/verify-iss36/')
GROUP BY src, t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Clicks by placement
panels.description:
Which control people actually press. blob4 carries the ?pos= parameter: 'inline' is the {{< book >}} shortcode in the prose, 'rail' is the sticky card beside the article above 900px, and 'bar' is the strip pinned to the bottom of the viewport below it (ISS-33, shipped 2026-08-20). 'rail' and 'bar' never appear on the same viewport, which is what makes the comparison between them meaningful -- below 900px the rail card is hidden rather than collapsed to the foot of the page, so no mobile click reports as 'rail'.

An empty or 'unknown' placement means a direct call to /go/airbnb, or a row written before the parameter existed on 2026-08-20.

Counts only clicks the Worker classified as coming from a browser, so the series starts on 2026-08-20. Rows written before that carry no verdict and are excluded rather than assumed human -- the two weeks before it are dominated by probes, DNS drain checks and crawler traffic, and there is no way to tell which of those rows were people. 'Recent clicks' is left unfiltered so the classifier can be audited.

targets.query:
SELECT
    if(blob4 IN ('', 'unknown'), 'no placement', blob4) AS placement,
    SUM(_sample_interval) AS clicks
FROM booking_clicks
WHERE $timeFilter AND blob5 = 'human' AND blob1 NOT IN ('/canary/', '/verify-iss36/')
GROUP BY placement
ORDER BY clicks DESC

defaults.noValue: No classified clicks in this range

panels.title: Page and placement
panels.description:
Where the click happened and which control did it. This is the pair that should decide where CTAs go -- a page with traffic and no clicks is a placement problem, not a content problem.

Counts only clicks the Worker classified as coming from a browser, so the series starts on 2026-08-20. Rows written before that carry no verdict and are excluded rather than assumed human -- the two weeks before it are dominated by probes, DNS drain checks and crawler traffic, and there is no way to tell which of those rows were people. 'Recent clicks' is left unfiltered so the classifier can be audited.

targets.query:
SELECT
    blob1 AS page,
    if(blob4 IN ('', 'unknown'), 'no placement', blob4) AS placement,
    SUM(_sample_interval) AS clicks
FROM booking_clicks
WHERE $timeFilter AND blob5 = 'human' AND blob1 NOT IN ('/canary/', '/verify-iss36/')
GROUP BY page, placement
ORDER BY clicks DESC

defaults.noValue: No classified clicks in this range

panels.title: Recent clicks
panels.description:
Every recorded click, unfiltered by verdict on purpose -- this is where you check whether the classifier is getting it right. Only the canary and the ISS-36 verification rows are removed.

An empty 'bot' column means the row predates classification (2026-08-20 23:37 UTC). An empty 'ua' or 'network' means the same.

This panel reads the Analytics Engine SQL API through Infinity rather than the ClickHouse plugin. The plugin pivots any result containing a DateTime column into one series per row, which is right for a graph and useless for a table, and it returns nothing at all when no numeric column is present -- which is why this panel showed nothing from the day it was written until 2026-08-20.

url_options.data: SELECT timestamp, blob1 AS src, blob4 AS pos, blob5 AS verdict, blob3 AS country, blob7 AS network, blob6 AS ua FROM booking_clicks WHERE timestamp >= toDateTime('${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}') AND timestamp <= toDateTime('${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}') AND blob1 NOT IN ('/canary/', '/verify-iss36/') ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 100 FORMAT JSON

panels.title: Visits, CTA clicks, and conversion rate
panels.description:
Booking clicks over visits, by day. The two numbers come from different APIs -- clicks from the booking_clicks Analytics Engine dataset, visits from Web Analytics over GraphQL -- and are joined here on the day.

Clicks are counted only when blob4 carries a placement, so probes, the daily canary and the DNS drain checks are excluded. That is why this panel reports far fewer clicks than 'Clicks in range' above, which excludes only the canary. It also means the series starts on 2026-08-20, when the placements shipped.

Visits exclude EU visitors entirely: the Web Analytics site is set to 'Enable, excluding visitor data in the EU'. The query also filters bot: 0, matching the 'Exclude bots' default in Cloudflare's own UI. That matters more than it sounds: on 2026-08-20 it took visits from 19 to 9, so leaving it out would have halved the reported conversion rate.

Known bias, and it runs one way. The visits denominator excludes bots (bot: 0). The clicks numerator does not: src/worker.js records every request to /go/airbnb regardless of what sent it, and crawlers do follow that link -- 27 clicks from ZA and 9 from NL in the fourteen days to 2026-08-20 arrived in bursts across many pages, seconds apart, with no referer. Fixed on 2026-08-20 (ISS-36): the Worker now records a verdict in blob5 and these panels exclude bots on both sides. Rows written before that carry no verdict and are not excluded, so any range reaching back past 2026-08-20 still overstates.

targets.query:
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(timestamp) AS day,
    SUM(_sample_interval) AS clicks
FROM booking_clicks
WHERE $timeFilter AND blob5 = 'human' AND blob1 NOT IN ('/canary/', '/verify-iss36/') AND blob4 NOT IN ('', 'unknown')
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day

defaults.noValue: No classified clicks in this range

panels.title: Conversion rate in range
panels.description:
Total CTA clicks divided by total visits over the selected range. Same filters as the panel to the left.

Do not believe this number yet. The placements shipped on 2026-08-20, so the only clicks it can see are from the same day, and most of them are ours from testing the rail. Six clicks against nine visits reads as 67 percent, which is not a conversion rate, it is us clicking our own button. It becomes meaningful once real traffic arrives and our own clicks stop being most of the numerator.

At this volume a single click moves it by several points regardless.

Known bias, and it runs one way. The visits denominator excludes bots (bot: 0). The clicks numerator does not: src/worker.js records every request to /go/airbnb regardless of what sent it, and crawlers do follow that link -- 27 clicks from ZA and 9 from NL in the fourteen days to 2026-08-20 arrived in bursts across many pages, seconds apart, with no referer. Fixed on 2026-08-20 (ISS-36): the Worker now records a verdict in blob5 and these panels exclude bots on both sides. Rows written before that carry no verdict and are not excluded, so any range reaching back past 2026-08-20 still overstates.
